title: What a missing act costs you
note: The page's three stacked bands, pillar, obligation and sunnah, each with the cost of leaving it written beside it.

lines.text: One of three ranks holds every Hajj act
Hajj is once in a life, in Dhul Hijjah
A pillar: leave it and there is no Hajj
lines.sub: money cannot buy a pillar back

lines.text: An obligation: a sacrifice repairs it
A sunnah: better, and nothing is owed
Only Arafah has no way back at all
The schools do not rank every act the same
lines.sub: sa'i: a pillar for three, a duty for Hanafi

lines.text: Read the row you were taught, not all four

lines.eyebrow: The three ranks, of the Hajj
lines.text: A dam is meat for the poor, not a fine
lines.sub: dam, a sacrifice: a sheep or a goat

research.retell: Every act of Hajj is ranked a pillar, an obligation, or a sunnah, and the schools do not always agree which act belongs in which band.
proof: Every act of the Hajj sits in one of three ranks, and the rank tells you what happens if it is missed.; what a missing act costs you
rukn, a pillar; wajib, an obligation; sunnah
rukn, a pillar: leave it and there is no Hajj; Rukn, pillar: the act is part of the thing itself. If you omit it, you have not performed the Hajj... Money cannot buy it back.
wajib, an obligation: a sacrifice repairs it; Wajib, obligation: the act is commanded but is not part of the essence. Omit it and the Hajj is valid, and a dam is due
sunnah: better, and nothing is owed; Sunnah: the Prophet ﷺ did it or encouraged it. Omitting it costs nothing but loses something. Most of what makes the Hajj beautiful lives here.
Only one act in the entire Hajj sits in the top band with no way back at all, and that is the standing at Arafah.
the schools do not all put the same act in the same band; Sa’i, seven between Safa and Marwah: Pillar for Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali; obligation for Hanafi.

Read across the row you were taught, not across all four at once. This table exists so that when a person in your group says the Hajj is only two things and another says it is five, you know that both of them are quoting a school and neither is inventing.
It literally means blood, and in these books it means a sacrifice, not a fine paid to anyone. It is meat for the poor of the sanctuary.; al-arkan wa al-wajibat, the pillars and the obligations
